name: MathlibAnnex.FiniteRecovery.targetRawSupportMaximizer_good
title: The chosen support slice consists of almost-isometric generators

content.display_title: The chosen support slice consists of almost-isometric generators
content.one_sentence_role: Obtains one almost-isometric map from each point of the specified raw maximum slice.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n=m+1>0$. Use reference coordinates $V=\mathbb R^n$ with the sup norm and standard basis. The supplied continuous seminorm $p$ has constants $a_p,b_p>0$ satisfying
$$a_p\|x\|_\infty\le p(x)\le b_p\|x\|_\infty\quad(x\in V).$$
Thus $p$ is a norm; it can differ from the reference sup norm. With standard Lebesgue measure $\lambda$ put $K_p=\{p\le1\}$ and $v_p=\lambda(K_p)>0$. For a real linear map $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$, its matrix is $A_{ij}=(Ae_j)_i$. The vector $\Pi_n(A)$ has coordinates $\Pi_n(A)_I=\det(A_{I,*})$, one for each increasing $n$-tuple $I$ of distinct rows. Define
$$\mathcal G_p^N=\left\{\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A):\begin{array}{l}A:V\to\mathbb R^N\text{ is real linear},\ \sigma\in\{1,-1\},\\ \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V)\end{array}\right\}.$$
A base family $F=(\ell_i)_{i=1}^n$ consists of real linear functionals on $V$. Put $M_F=(\ell_i(e_j))$. Let $\mathcal U_p=\{F:\forall i,x,\ |\ell_i(x)|\le p(x)\}$ and
$$D_p=\max_{F\in\mathcal U_p}|\det M_F|,\qquad
\mathcal N_{p,\eta}=\{F\in\mathcal U_p:D_p-\eta\le|\det M_F|\}.$$
Fix $0\le\eta<D_p$, $\varepsilon>0$, and one $K>0$ such that $p(M_F^{-1}c)\le K\|c\|_\infty$ for all $F\in\mathcal N_{p,\eta}$ and all $c\in V$. Set
$$\rho=\min(\varepsilon,1)/(8K),\qquad
\mathcal A_K=\{c:1/K\le\|c\|_\infty\le1\}.$$
Take a finite $C_{\mathrm{net}}\subset\mathcal A_K$ covering that annulus at sup-distance at most $\rho$; its center $a$ gives $c_a=a$. Fix $w>0$ with
$$D_p\sum_{a\in C_{\mathrm{net}}}\sum_i|(c_a)_i|<w\eta.$$
For a family of real linear functionals $s=(s_a)_{a\in C_{\mathrm{net}}}$, call $Q=(F,s)$ admissible when $F\in\mathcal U_p$ and $|s_a(x)|\le p(x)$ for all $a,x$. For this configuration put
$$\Phi_{w,c}(Q)=w\det M_F+\sum_a\sum_i(c_a)_i\det M_F[i\leftarrow s_a].$$
Here the replaced row is $(s_a(e_j))_j$. Put $N=n+|C_{\mathrm{net}}|$. In minor space let $I_0$ select the base rows and $I_{i,a}$ select all base rows except $i$, then satellite $a$, and let $e_I$ be the corresponding minor-coordinate unit vector. Define
$$\Omega_{w,c}=we_{I_0}+\sum_a\sum_i(c_a)_i(-1)^{n-i}e_{I_{i,a}}.$$
Choose an admissible absolute maximizer $Q_*$ of $\Phi_{w,c}$. Set $\theta=1$ if $\Phi_{w,c}(Q_*)\ge0$ and $\theta=-1$ otherwise, and define the linear functional $\ell(z)=\theta\langle\Omega_{w,c},z\rangle$ ([oriented support](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L415-L420)). If
$$z\in \mathcal G_p^N,\qquad \ell(z)=\max_{u\in \mathcal G_p^N}\ell(u),$$
then one real linear $A:V\to\mathbb R^N$ satisfies
$$\forall x,\ \|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x),\qquad
\forall x\ (p(x)=1),\ 1-\varepsilon<\|Ax\|_\infty,$$
$$z=\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A)\quad\text{for some }\sigma\in\{1,-1\}.$$
content.assumptions: The inputs are the continuous norm $p$ with the displayed comparison bounds; $0\le\eta<D_p$; $\varepsilon>0$; the common inverse bound $K>0$; the stated finite net at radius $\rho$; $w>0$; the strict budget; and a point $z$ in the displayed maximum slice of $\mathcal G_p^N$. All rows in the admissible configurations are real linear functionals. There is no assumption $\varepsilon<1$.
content.conclusion: One $A$ has all three properties. For each unit vector the detecting satellite index may vary, while the map is fixed first.
content.proof_summary: Recover the same generating map, transfer support maximality to absolute polynomial maximality, and use the finite-net estimate.

proof_steps.text:
**Recover the same map and compare both support values.** Membership in $\mathcal G_p^N$ supplies one real linear $A$ and $\sigma\in\{1,-1\}$ with
$$\|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)\quad(x\in V),\qquad z=\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A).$$
Extract the base and satellite rows of $A$ as $Q=(F,s)$. With the base coordinates followed by the enumerated satellite coordinates,
$$A_{(F,s)}x=((\ell_i(x))_{i=1}^n,(s_b(x))_{b\in C_{\mathrm{net}}}).$$
Their individual bounds make $Q$ admissible, and the [extraction identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L529-L542) gives $A_{(F,s)}=A$. The [normalized pairing identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L390-L398) and its [oriented form](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L422-L438) yield
$$\begin{aligned}
\ell(z)&=\sigma v_p\theta\Phi_{w,c}(Q)\\
&\le v_p|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|\\
&\le v_p|\Phi_{w,c}(Q_*)|.
\end{aligned}$$
For the reverse inequality, use the raw generator $v_p\Pi_n(A_{Q_*})$ with no extra sign. It belongs to $\mathcal G_p^N$, and
$$\begin{aligned}
\ell\bigl(v_p\Pi_n(A_{Q_*})\bigr)
 &=v_p\theta\Phi_{w,c}(Q_*)\\
 &=v_p|\Phi_{w,c}(Q_*)|\\
 &\le\ell(z).
\end{aligned}$$
The middle equality is [the support value at its chosen configuration](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/PluckerSupport.lean#L440-L447); the last is precisely maximality of $z$. Hence both inequalities in the first chain are equalities. Since $v_p>0$,
$$|\Phi_{w,c}(Q)|=|\Phi_{w,c}(Q_*)|.$$
This is [raw support-to-configuration recovery](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteRecovery.lean#L362-L515) for the original generating map $A$.

**Apply finite-net detection to that configuration.** For every fixed $x$ with $p(x)=1$, the required output is
$$\exists a\in C_{\mathrm{net}},\qquad 1-\varepsilon<|s_a(x)|.$$
Apply [the finite-net estimate for an absolute maximizer](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Dual/Satellite.lean#L1045-L1066) with the same $p,\eta,\varepsilon,K,C_{\mathrm{net}},w$ and the same configuration $Q$. The inverse bound, net radius and strict budget are the stated inputs. Admissibility and absolute maximality of $Q$ were established in Step 1. Only the detecting index $a$ may depend on $x$; the map $A$ remains fixed.

**Read the detecting functional as a coordinate of the fixed map.** Fix $x$ with $p(x)=1$, and choose the index $a$ supplied by Step 2. The map in Step 1 has the coordinate vector
$$Ax=A_{(F,s)}x=
 ((\ell_i(x))_{i=1}^n,(s_b(x))_{b\in C_{\mathrm{net}}}).$$
Consequently its sup norm is
$$\|Ax\|_\infty=
\max\left(\{ |\ell_i(x)|:1\le i\le n\}
 \cup\{ |s_b(x)|:b\in C_{\mathrm{net}}\}\right).$$
The union is nonempty because $n>0$. Since $a\in C_{\mathrm{net}}$, the particular value $|s_a(x)|$ is one of the values in this maximum. This is the [satellite-coordinate identity](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteSup.lean#L475-L479), applied to $Q=(F,s)$ and this same $a,x$, together with the defining property of the sup norm. Substituting the strict estimate from Step 2 therefore gives
$$1-\varepsilon<|s_a(x)|\le\|Ax\|_\infty\le p(x)=1.$$
The last inequality is the original contractivity from Step 1. The argument applies to every $x$ with $p(x)=1$; only $a$ depends on $x$. Thus the original $A$ is contractive and has the asserted strict lower bound on the unit sphere, while its original representation $z=\sigma v_p\Pi_n(A)$ is unchanged. These are precisely the three conditions in [the good-generator RHS](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Normed/Operator/FiniteRecovery.lean#L326-L331).

content.lean_realization_notes: The sign $\theta$ belongs to the fixed functional $\ell$, whereas $\sigma$ represents the input raw generator. They have different roles. The raw set is [compact](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L67-L90) and [nonempty](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Convex/PluckerBody.lean#L30-L32); its convex hull is the Plücker body. The hypothesis here concerns the raw maximum slice itself, not an arbitrary point of that convex hull.
